jobs.title: Director, AI Governance & Enablement
jobs.description:
We are hiring a Director, AI Governance & Enablement on behalf of a well-established organization in Mississauga.

In your new role as a Director, AI Governance & Enablement, you will be accountable for operating and advancing company’s enterprise AI practice. The role exists to help the organization adopt AI safely, practically, and at scale by combining governance discipline with education, advisory support, and pragmatic implementation guidance. It is not a research or data science role.

You will operate the governance processes that determine how AI is introduced into day-to-day work, help departments identify and prioritize valuable AI use cases, and ensure AI systems are deployed responsibly as they become more multimodal, more connected to enterprise data, and more capable of influencing decisions, workflows, and user behaviour. The role also serves as AI expertise-as-a-service function, working across corporate departments, FASTech, Service Management & Automation, Business Analysis & Quality Assurance, Data & Analytics, Privacy, Cybersecurity, and enterprise applications so that AI-enabled solutions are useful, explainable, governable, and aligned to operational realities.

The position has no direct reports. Authority is exercised through ownership of enterprise AI governance processes, leadership of the AI enablement program portfolio, management of third-party AI partner relationships, and cross-functional influence rather than direct supervision. The role owns the working relationship with external AI platform providers, training partners, and advisory firms — holding them to company’s governance, privacy, and security expectations, and leveraging them to extend internal AI education and enablement capacity. Governance framework design, risk-tier definitions, and final approval authority for higher-risk AI initiatives rest with the Director, Innovation & Technology Enablement; this role recommends, operates, and enforces.

Key Accountabilities

Enterprise AI Governance

Recommend, maintain, and continuously improve AI governance framework, standards, guardrails, and acceptable-use practices in alignment with legal, privacy, security, and risk requirements, escalating framework changes to the Director for approval.
Apply and document practical controls for responsible AI use, including human accountability, override mechanisms, confidence thresholds, auditability, data handling expectations, and documentation standards.
Operate the AI intake and review process end to end — triage, assessment, and recommendation on appropriateness, value, risk, explainability, and organizational readiness.
Apply established risk classification and approval paths, distinguishing between low-risk productivity uses, operational decision support, and higher-risk use cases, and route initiatives above the defined threshold to the Director for decision.
Partner with Privacy, Cybersecurity, Legal, and enterprise technology leaders to ensure AI-enabled solutions meet policy, compliance, and audit expectations.
Define and apply governance expectations for third-party AI providers and partners, including data handling, model transparency, sub-processor disclosure, and alignment to company’s privacy and security requirements, working with Privacy, Cybersecurity, Legal, and Procurement.

AI Education & Organizational Readiness

Design and deliver role-based AI education, awareness, and training programs for leaders, practitioners, and end users.
Create and maintain practical playbooks, templates, examples, and decision guides that help teams use AI effectively and responsibly.
Promote AI literacy across the organization by translating technical concepts into plain-language guidance and actionable practices.
Support leaders in understanding the opportunities and risks of multimodal AI, connected AI, agentic workflows, and AI-assisted decision support.
Track adoption, usage patterns, and learning outcomes to refine enablement programs and improve organizational readiness.
Manage third-party training and enablement partners, including scope, delivery quality, and alignment of externally sourced content to Chartwell’s AI standards and governance expectations.

AI Expertise-as-a-Service (Advisory)

Provide advisory support to corporate departments on AI opportunities, use-case framing, vendor and tool evaluation, and solution options.
Help teams convert ambiguous problems into clear AI and automation use cases with defined objectives, constraints, risks, and success measures.
Support business and technology teams during design and implementation with practical guidance on model and tool selection, workflow design, prompting patterns, and integration considerations.
Act as a trusted internal partner who helps departments move from experimentation to controlled, business-aligned AI adoption.
Contribute expert guidance to FASTech and other delivery teams so that AI-enabled solutions remain practical, supportable, and aligned with enterprise standards.

Safeguarding the Organization as AI Evolves

Develop guidance and control patterns for AI systems that use text, images, documents, screenshots, voice, and other multimodal inputs or outputs.
Apply governance to AI systems connected to enterprise data sources, documents, communications, applications, and external research tools.
Assess and mitigate risks related to hallucinations, model drift, privacy invasion, data leakage, bias, impersonation, surveillance, over-reliance, and unsafe automation.
Recommend boundaries for where AI may assist versus where decisions must remain deterministic or human-owned, especially for safety, compliance, financial approvals, and resident-impacting decisions.
Provide guidance on the safe use of AI as an assistant, coach, or decision-support tool, including controls to prevent manipulation, inappropriate inference, or hidden monitoring behaviours.

Program Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Lead the AI enablement program portfolio, including planning, sequencing, stakeholder coordination, and delivery tracking against committed outcomes.
Work closely with FASTech, Service Management & Automation, Business Analysis & Quality Assurance, Data & Analytics, Cybersecurity, enterprise applications, and business leaders to align AI adoption with business priorities.
Own the ongoing working relationship with third-party AI platform providers, advisory firms, and education partners, including roadmap awareness, escalation paths, and periodic performance and risk review.
Maintain the enterprise register of approved AI use cases, tools, integrations, risks, and realized outcomes.
Prepare executive reporting on AI pipeline, enablement activities, governance findings, adoption levels, and realized value for presentation by the Director.
Identify recurring themes, risks, and opportunities across departments and recommend pragmatic improvements to AI operating model.

Qualifications

Education

Post-secondary education in Computer Science, Data, Information Systems, Business, Risk, Privacy, or a related discipline is preferred.
Demonstrated and credible expertise in AI governance, responsible AI, and enterprise AI enablement will be strongly considered in lieu of a formal degree.
Coursework, certifications, or professional development in AI governance, privacy, risk, responsible AI, or change management are assets.

Experience

8+ years of progressive professional experience in technology, digital transformation, technology advisory, or a closely related field.
5+ years of combined, demonstrable experience across AI governance, AI adoption and enablement, people enablement and training, and hands-on AI solution development.
Demonstrated experience establishing or operating governance, standards, or policy controls for enterprise technology or AI adoption.
Experience designing and delivering training, communications, and change readiness programs for technology adoption.
Practical working experience with large language models, copilots, AI agents, multimodal AI, and AI systems connected to enterprise data and workflows, including hands-on prototyping or solution build.
Experience leading programs or workstreams to delivery without direct authority over contributors.
Experience operating in a mid-sized, decentralized, multi-site environment is an asset; exposure to seniors housing, real estate, healthcare delivery, retail, or hospitality operations is an asset.

Skills & Abilities

Communication:
Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to translate technical concepts into clear guidance for business leaders and end users.
Influence & Facilitation:
Strong facilitation, stakeholder management, and influence skills across functions and levels, including the ability to hold a governance position under pressure while maintaining constructive working relationships.
Risk Judgement:
Pragmatic risk management mindset with the ability to balance innovation with restraint.
Technology Assessment:
Ability to assess emerging AI capabilities and convert them into practical organizational guidance and standards.
Program Discipline:
Structured approach to planning, documentation, and delivery tracking so that enablement commitments are measurable and auditable.

The Director will translate business priorities into a practical architectural vision and roadmap that enables exceptional client service, operational effectiveness, innovation and secure, sustainable growth.

jobs.description:
Join CoolIT, an Ecolab Company, a global leader in Direct Liquid Cooling technology for data centers, supercomputers, and high-performance computing environments.

As our Director, Business Engagement Leader for CoolIT
, you will be the senior technology leader co-located with the CoolIT business and the single point of accountability between CoolIT’s leadership team and Ecolab’s Enterprise AI and Digital organization. You will fuel one of the most ambitious growth stories in Ecolab with technology-, data-, and AI-enabled business outcomes while confidently integrating CoolIT into Ecolab’s IT security, compliance, and technology strategy.

You will be accountable for delivering solutions from idea through value capture, ensuring growth is never held back by technology or put at risk by it.

This is not a typical IT engagement role. As AI data centers shift from air to liquid cooling, demand for CoolIT’s technology is surging. The business is adding people, products, suppliers, and manufacturing capacity at a pace few companies experience. At the same time, CoolIT is becoming part of a NYSE-listed global enterprise with mature expectations for cybersecurity, compliance, and technology governance.

This role requires a leader who can operate at CoolIT speed while drawing on Ecolab’s enterprise strength. You will anticipate where the business is heading, make sound decisions with incomplete information, remove blockers quickly, and balance fit-for-purpose solutions with long-term technology strategy. As a trusted translator between CoolIT’s entrepreneurial, engineering-led culture and Ecolab’s enterprise operating model, you will protect what makes CoolIT fast while introducing the platforms, shared services, security, and governance needed to support sustainable growth.

What’s In It For You

Lead the Enterprise AI agenda for CoolIT, the business at the heart of Ecolab’s AI data center strategy and a cornerstone of its largest growth engine.
Own end-to-end delivery of AI, data, and digital solutions that help CoolIT scale engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain operations to meet hyperscale demand.
Partner directly with CoolIT executives and Ecolab Enterprise AI leaders as a trusted, commercially minded technology advisor.
Shape a defining integration, establishing how a high-growth acquisition adopts Ecolab platforms, security, and governance without losing its speed.
Influence enterprise-wide AI and digital strategy while owning technology outcomes that support CoolIT’s growth. Help develop a business engagement model that Ecolab can extend to other businesses.
Help build and lead a dedicated CoolIT technology team, providing leadership through influence across CoolIT-specific enterprise architecture and infrastructure roles.
Work in a hybrid environment.

What You Will Do

Build strong partnerships with CoolIT’s executive team and leaders across commercial, engineering, operations, supply chain, quality, and finance to understand growth ambitions and operational pressure points.
Align Ecolab’s technology strategy with CoolIT’s growth plan, using technology, AI, and analytics to scale capacity, accelerate customer delivery, protect margins, and ensure systems, infrastructure, data, support, and end-to-end business processes are ready before they are needed.
Own the delivery of CoolIT technology solutions from demand intake and business case development through design, build, deployment, adoption, and value realization.
Hold Ecolab delivery teams, partners, and local stakeholders accountable for outcomes, schedules, costs, and quality; remove blockers quickly; and ensure committed business value is captured and reported.
Drive the technology integration roadmap that brings CoolIT onto Ecolab platforms and shared services at a pace the business can absorb, determining what to adopt, adapt, or temporarily retain so integration supports rather than interrupts growth.
Work with CoolIT leadership and finance to establish appropriate technology and AI investment levels and recommend investments, cost optimization opportunities, and resource allocations that maximize commercial value and return on investment.
Serve as the primary point of contact for CoolIT leaders on Enterprise AI, data, digital, and IT matters, managing expectations and resolving systemic issues, escalations, and enhancement requests across applications, infrastructure, and digital services.
Oversee IT services and support for CoolIT’s offices, engineering labs, and manufacturing sites; track service levels; drive continuous improvement; and escalate issues affecting production, customer commitments, or business growth.
Bring visibility and disciplined prioritization to CoolIT’s technology portfolio by assessing requests before PMO intake, confirming budget and business-resource readiness, securing delivery capacity, and keeping Enterprise AI resources focused on the highest-value work.
Ensure CoolIT projects receive Ecolab Security and Enterprise Architecture approval and partner with Ecolab Cybersecurity to close integration gaps across identity, endpoints, networks, cloud services, manufacturing systems, and third-party access.
Embed Ecolab policies, controls, and audit-readiness requirements, including SOX IT general controls, data privacy, and customer security assurance, while protecting CoolIT’s intellectual property and confidential customer and partner information.
Lead, coach, and develop a CoolIT-dedicated technology team, providing dotted-line leadership to CoolIT’s Enterprise Architect and infrastructure support roles and managing through influence across the broader Enterprise AI organization.

Travel: Regular travel to CoolIT manufacturing, engineering, and supplier sites, including locations in Asia; periodic travel to Ecolab locations in the United States for Enterprise AI leadership engagements.
Reporting line: Solid-line reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise AI – Global Markets within Ecolab’s Enterprise AI organization, with a dotted-line relationship to CoolIT business leadership and close day-to-day partnership with the CoolIT leadership team.

Demonstrated accountability and a track record of delivering major technology programs in a fast-growing, multi-site manufacturing, engineering, or high-technology environment.

jobs.description:
BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

Role Summary

The Director, Non-Financial Risk Assessment Programs leads how Capital Markets carries out BMO's main non-financial risk identification and assessment programs: PRC (Process, Risk & Control) and Risk ID inventories and RCSA (Risk & Control Self-Assessment) and RCRAs (Regulatory Compliance Risk Assessment). The Director is the main point of coordination between the first line (1LOD) Business Control teams and the second line (2LOD) enterprise program owners. They make sure assessments are accurate, defensible, delivered on time, and meet ONFR and ECP requirements.

The Director brings a deep understanding of how risks, controls, processes, products, business units and legal entities connect across Capital Markets. They advocate with enterprise program owners for structures and methodologies that fit the business. The role improves inventory quality, makes execution consistent across business units (BUs), reduces the workload on Business Controls and Business Units and improves portfolio level assessments

Key Accountabilities

Inventory governance and PRC management
Own year-round governance and data-quality oversight of BU PRC inventories (products and services, internal activities, processes, specific risks and controls).
Lead the annual PRC Inventory Confirmation.
Manage organizational and ownership changes, including BU realignments, lift-and-shifts, new inventory builds, MCC/ME updates and inventory rationalization.
Monitor inventory health through Risk Mart and Power BI. Find missing attributes, linkages and data-quality issues, then drive remediation and escalate unresolved gaps.
Make sure applicable Master Common Controls (MCCs) and shared controls are adopted correctly in BU control inventories, including SOX designations.
Capital Markets risk structure and cross-program linkages
Act as the authoritative interpreter of PRC, RCSA, RCRA for Capital Markets.
Act as Capital Markets' expert on how products and services, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities connect, and keep that view current as the business and organization change.
Advocate with the enterprise program owner for the data structure, taxonomy and linkage design that best fits Capital Markets, including how KRIs, Issues and Events connect to PRC risk and control records.
Give business requirements and practical input on changes to the GRCE data model, workflow and future-state integration, including aggregation at the Legal Entity level.
Make sure Capital Markets inventories apply the agreed linkage standards consistently. This includes keeping Issues linked to Key Controls complete and accurate
Find structural gaps or misalignments, such as missing, orphaned or inconsistent linkages, and bring them to the program owner with recommended fixes.
Use the linked data to support RCSA residual risk ratings, overrides and Targeted Risk Evaluations (TREs) with evidence, and to show where control weaknesses, KRI breaches and loss events cluster.
Risk assessment execution (RCSA and RCRA)
Lead the PRC/RCSA/RCRA Annual Plan.
Oversee risk categorization (key vs. non-key) and ensure assessments are right sized taking a risk based approach.
Oversee reviews of TREs, including inherent risk, control effectiveness, residual risk, overrides and rationales. Ensure High Residual Risk ratings have corrective actions to improve control effectiveness.
Lead RCRA execution and work with Business Regulatory Control teams to maintain and accurate inventory of risk evaluation points (REPs). Reconcile RCRA results with the regulatory and privacy TREs in the RCSA so regulatory compliance risk feeds into the BU risk profile.
Manage slippage and deferral requests, and exception and exemption requests, in line with Directive requirements.
Coordinate Effective Challenge from Operational Risk Officers (OROs), Risk Specialty Areas (RSAs), Enterprise Control Functions (ECFs) and other programs. Track comments, how they're resolved, and due dates.
Advocacy with 2LOD program owners
Act as Capital Markets' lead advocate with the 2LOD program owners (ONFR, ECP and Regulatory Compliance, and Risk Specialty Areas). Represent the business's interests in methodology, Policy, Standard & Procedure changes.
Influence program design so requirements suit Capital Markets' products, trading activities and legal entity structure and aid towards reducing risk.
Negotiate realistic timelines, scope and sequencing for program deliverables. Prepare well- supported rationale for exceptions, exemptions or alternative approaches when they're justified.
Bring the business's perspective, practical constraints and lessons learned to enterprise working groups and consultations. Share upcoming program changes with Director, Risk Programs for inclusion in broader communications across Capital Markets.
Build trusted, credible relationships with 2LOD so issues are resolved collaboratively and escalated only when needed.
Reporting and executive enablement
Produce AE summary materials and approval packages, and keep approval evidence in GRCE.
Provide risk profile insights and committee reporting (for example, VRC).
Continuous improvement and future-state capability
Lead improvements to methodology, process, reporting and systems with ONFR. Standardize tools, templates and procedures.
Represent Capital Markets in working groups, user acceptance testing (UAT) and platform evaluations to shape GRCE and future assessment capabilities.
People leadership
Lead, develop and set priorities for team members and Business Control teams across concurrent assessment cycles.
Build a culture of accountability, data quality and practical, business-friendly risk partnership.

Key relationships

1LOD: Business Controls, Risk Domain Leads, Business Unit Leads, Accountable Executives, Operational Resilience & Risk Programs, Portfolio Analytics, Capital Markets Assurance Role, Enterprise Control Functions
2LOD: ONFR and ECP program & methodology owners, OROs, RSAs, Regulatory Compliance and Privacy

Qualifications

10+ years in operational or non-financial risk, risk and control self-assessment, or governance at a large financial institution, including people leadership. Capital Markets experience strongly preferred.
Deep understanding of how Capital Markets products, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities relate, and the ability to turn that into clear structural requirements for enterprise program owners.
Deep knowledge of the three lines of defence model, risk and control taxonomies, residual risk methods and Effective Challenge.
Proven ability to influence and negotiate with 2LOD and enterprise program owners, representing business interests credibly and constructively.
Hands-on experience with a GRC platform (Archer preferred) and with data and reporting tools (Power BI, Risk Mart).
Track record of leading enterprise programs on regulatory deadlines and producing audit- ready, AE-ready and committee-ready materials.
Strong judgment and executive presence, and the ability to escalate issues diplomatically with senior stakeholders.

jobs.description:

You will drive operational excellence across cloud platforms, developer tooling, application security, and technology operations while partnering closely with Engineering, Product, and Security leaders.

In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To

About Solink

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most
. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster
by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

Our cloud-based platform integrates seamlessly with your existing cameras and systems, turning them into intelligent sensors that detect and interpret key moments. This empowers teams to make data-driven decisions, enhance security, and improve operational efficiency.

Trusted by over 36,000 locations across 60+ countries - including brands like McDonald’s and JYSK - Solink delivers clarity when it counts. Our solutions help businesses reduce shrink, optimize performance, and respond proactively to potential threats.

We're growing rapidly, earning industry recognition, and scaling with purpose. We’ve been recognized by Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, Business Intelligence Group, and as one of Ottawa’s Best Places to Work. And we’re just getting started!

The Role

Solink is hiring a Director of Solutions Engineering
to lead our two Solutions Engineering teams, covering SMB through Enterprise, and build a high-performing pre-sales technical organization across Solink’s software and hardware solutions.

You will own how Solink engages customers technically throughout the sales process, from discovery and solution design through demos, pilots, technical validation, and technical close. Your SEs will be the technical leaders of the deal and speak the language of the customer—the priorities, workflows, and challenges of each industry and persona we serve.

This role reports to the Senior Vice President of Revenue and partners closely with Sales, Product, Customer Success, Channel, and Implementation. The role will include occasional travel to events and customer sites across North America.

What You’ll Do

Lead the SE Organization: Lead, coach, and develop two SE teams and their leaders, with clear expectations, career paths, and performance standards. Run a consistent operating model across segments and focus SE capacity on the highest-value and most complex opportunities.
Drive Technical Sales Execution: Oversee technical discovery, solution design, demos, workshops, objection handling, competitive positioning, technical validation, closing, and clean handoff across the sales organization.
Build a World-Class Demo and Storytelling Culture: Set the standard for how Solink demonstrates its platform through customer use cases and business outcomes. Build repeatable demo frameworks and talk tracks by vertical and persona, and coach SEs on storytelling, executive presence, and technical credibility.
Design Solutions That Can Be Deployed: Ensure solutions account for customer camera, recorder, network, and POS infrastructure, including hardware needs, appliance sizing, bandwidth planning, site readiness, and deployment requirements.
Lead Technical Workshops & Pilots: Lead architecture discussions, site surveys, RFPs, security and compliance reviews, and pilot design, with clear success criteria and a path to full deployment.
Scale Technical Capability Beyond the SE Team: Partner with Sales Enablement to raise AE technical competency, help channel partners and installers become more technically self-sufficient, and define when partner-led scoping and installation is appropriate.
Partner with Product: Build a strong feedback loop with Product around recurring customer requirements, technical gaps, competitive intelligence, and field readiness for new launches.

Role Expectations

This is an M4
level role. At Solink, leaders at this level are accountable for leading through managers and driving the execution of significant initiatives across their area. They operate with a high degree of autonomy, translate strategy into clear priorities for their teams, and partner with senior leaders to solve complex problems and make effective decisions.

In this role, you’ll be expected to:

Set clear priorities and operating expectations across the Solutions Engineering organization, aligning team capacity and execution with broader Sales and company goals.
Lead and develop SE leaders and teams, creating accountability for performance while building capability, career growth, and succession within the organization.
Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives that improve technical sales execution, customer experience, and the scalability of the Solutions Engineering function.
Identify technical, operational, and capacity challenges early, develop thoughtful solutions, and proactively resolve dependencies across Sales, Product, Channel, Customer Success, and Implementation.
Use business and team performance metrics to evaluate SE effectiveness, prioritize investments, and make decisions that improve deal progression, technical quality, and organizational efficiency.
Drive adoption of new processes, tools, and ways of working while creating a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and high performance.

What Success Looks Like

Solutions Engineering operates with a clear and consistent model across SMB through Enterprise, with strong leadership, clear ownership, and effective allocation of SE capacity.
SE teams consistently deliver high-quality technical discovery, demos, solution designs, pilots, and handoffs that support strong sales outcomes and predictable deployment.
Customers receive compelling, persona- and industry-specific technical experiences that clearly connect Solink’s capabilities to their business needs and outcomes.
AEs and channel partners have stronger technical capability and know when and how to engage Solutions Engineering to maximize deal outcomes.
Solution designs can be deployed as sold, improving implementation predictability, customer experience, and margin protection.
The Solutions Engineering organization continuously improves through better processes, feedback loops, technical standards, and an AI-first approach that can scale with the business.

These outcomes are directly grounded in the source JD’s stated success measures, particularly around operating consistency, demo quality, deployable solutions, increased AE/partner capability, and an AI-first approach.

What You Bring

Must-Have:

Experienced Solutions Engineering Leader: You bring 8+ years of experience in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, or Solutions Architecture, including 3+ years leading leaders.
Complex Technical Sales Experience: You have experience supporting complex B2B SaaS or technical sales within enterprise and multi-location environments.

Top Aces is seeking a Director, IT Enterprise Applications, to lead the strategy, modernization and performance of our core business applications supporting Fleet management, flight planning, MRO, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Finance, Human Resources and Operations.

This is more than an application support role. You will work directly with business leaders to improve processes, strengthen critical platforms, simplify our application landscape and help shape the future of enterprise technology at Top Aces.

Proven experience with ERP modernization and business-process transformation.
Experience managing complex enterprise application portfolios and vendors.
Strong understanding of ERP, integrations, APIs, application lifecycle management and IT service management.

Top Aces moves from fragmented applications and manual workarounds toward a simplified, integrated and resilient enterprise application ecosystem that improves mission readiness, operational efficiency and global scalability.

Beem Credit Union: Banking for every journey

Beem is redefining what it means to be a credit union. With 80 years of cooperative history and a bold vision for the future, we’ve united to create a financial partner that offers both digital ease and people-first service.

Our mission is clear: financial wellness for all.
We help British Columbians achieve their goals through personalized advice, innovative technology, and genuine human connection.

As one of BC’s largest credit unions, we serve over 200,000 members
across 66 branches
with $18 billion in assets under administration
.

If you’re passionate about making a difference and want to join a team that values collaboration, innovation, and purpose, join us on the journey.

Learn more: www.beemcreditunion.ca

What this role is all about:

Reporting to the VP, Digital Solutions, the Director, Application Services
is a senior technology leader accountable for the health, reliability, performance and ongoing evolution of Beem’s enterprise-wide Application Services portfolio, which includes core banking, lending, digital banking, enterprise applications, and other assigned business applications. The role ensures these applications remain secure, resilient, current and well supported, providing a dependable and scalable foundation for Beem’s members, employees and business operations. The Director sets the multi-year strategic direction for Application Services and owns the operating model, investment priorities and portfolio decisions within their accountability, shaping how applications are managed and evolved across Beem.

The Director leads multiple teams responsible for application support, configuration, upgrades, patching and testing, operational vendor management, and delivery of small non-material enhancements. The role translates Business and Technology priorities into coordinated application service and lifecycle plans, balancing operational excellence with application simplification, automation, responsible AI and continuous improvement to reduce friction, improve efficiency and enable Beem’s digital-first and people-first ambitions.

This is a hybrid position, and preference will be given to applicants located in British Columbia. In-person interview(s) will be required during the later stages of the recruitment process, with location(s) to be determined.

What you’ll do:

Leadership and Team Success

As a member of the Technology Leadership team, accountability for the decisions connecting application services priorities to member outcomes, business needs and Beem’s strategic direction.
Leads Beem’s Application Services portfolio, building high-performing teams and establishing clear accountability and service ownership across the applications, while fostering collaboration, curiosity and continuous improvement.
Owns the Application Services operating model, organizational structure, budget, and service ownership model, including the allocation of leadership accountability across teams and managers, and evolves the model as Beem’s application portfolio and strategic priorities change.
Builds workforce capability in application service management, digital platforms, automation and responsible AI, supported by coaching, career pathways, succession planning and knowledge sharing.
Aligns team capacity and skills to operational commitments, lifecycle requirements and approved change priorities, making trade-offs visible and escalating constraints before delivery or service is affected.
Maintains sustainable support coverage, including extended-hours and on-call arrangements for critical services, while reducing key-person dependencies and supporting employee well-being.

Application Services & Operational Resilience

Owns the operational health of applications in scope, establishing service expectations and monitoring that reflect business criticality, member journeys and employee needs.
Leads application incident and problem management in partnership with Technology Operations, the Service Desk and vendors, restoring service promptly and addressing root causes to prevent recurrence.
Oversees application configuration and administration, including product and rate setup, workflows, business rules and in-application access, supported by appropriate approvals, testing and controls.
Strengthens application observability, runbooks, known-error records and knowledge practices to identify issues earlier and improve first-contact resolution.
Partners with business continuity, disaster recovery and Technology teams to validate application recovery readiness, test critical dependencies and address resilience gaps.

Application Lifecycle & Change Delivery

Develops and maintains an enterprise-wide rolling multi-year application service and lifecycle roadmap aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture and technology plans, balancing currency, resilience, supportability and cost.
Provides recommendations on application consolidation, retirement and standardization to reduce duplication, technical debt and operational complexity, with investment and architecture decisions made through established governance.
Leads vendor upgrades and patches through impact assessment, regression testing, cutover and stabilization, maintaining visibility into version currency, end-of-support exposure and remediation plans.
Delivers configuration changes and small enhancements on non-material initiatives, coordinating dependencies, release readiness and stakeholder communication to minimize member and employee disruption.
Establishes mandatory operational acceptance criteria for new or materially changed applications and has authority to withhold operational acceptance where service readiness, resilience, supportability or control requirements have not been met.

AI, Automation & Continuous Improvement

Develops and prioritizes a practical improvement backlog using service data, incident trends and member and employee feedback, focusing on reduced friction, reliability and measurable operational value.
Introduces approved AI-enabled and automated practices for activities such as ticket triage, knowledge management, release analysis and regression testing, with human accountability and appropriate oversight.
Partners with business owners, Enterprise Transformation & Integration, and Technology teams to translate process improvements into supportable application changes, while preserving clear business, delivery and operational accountabilities.
Measures whether improvements reduce manual effort, recurring demand and service delays, and redirects released capacity toward higher-value work and priority commitments.

Business Partnership, Risk & Vendor Management

Groupe INVESTIIR

Saint-Hubert (Longueuil)
Temps plein
150 000 $ + partage des profits
Relève du directeur général
Entrée en poste en janvier

On cherche un partenaire qui pilote la finance, pas seulement un comptable.

Qui on est

Chez Groupe INVESTIIR, on bâtit l'avenir des gens en simplifiant l'accès à la propriété. Depuis Saint-Hubert, on développe et on vend des terrains et des chalets dans Lanaudière et les Laurentides — et on est verticalement intégrés : on achète le terrain, on le lotit, on construit les rues, on bâtit les chalets, on les vend et on accompagne nos clients jusqu'à la location. Tout sous le même toit. On dirige avec EOS : des rôles clairs, des mesurables chaque semaine, une imputabilité assumée. Et quand on est profitables, on partage le profit avec toute l'équipe.

Pourquoi ce poste existe

On structure le groupe pour sa prochaine étape : un comité de direction, des revenus récurrents, et des systèmes qui roulent sans le fondateur. Aujourd'hui, le cash, les prêteurs et le fonds de prêt passent encore par le président. Tu prends ça en main — finance, RH et légal de plusieurs sociétés — avec un siège au comité de direction.

Ce que gagner veut dire

Chaque semaine, les chiffres du Groupe sont véridiques et comptabilisés — on peut dire à l'équipe, avec précision, où en est le partage des profits — et la finance, les RH et le légal roulent sans le président. Tu livres la conciliation et la prévision de cash sur 13 semaines de chaque entité, avec moins de 5 % d'écart sur le réel. Tu pilotes la dette et le fonds de prêt — prêteurs, remboursements, nouveaux prêts. Tu fais vivre le contrôle des dépenses (aucune dépense sans PO), tu mènes la fermeture mensuelle et tu portes notre relation avec les fournisseurs. Tu pilotes les RH : paie, partage des profits, dossiers d'employés. Tu pilotes le légal et la fiscalité avec notre conseiller juridique et nos professionnels externes.

Ton équipe

Un responsable finance, une technicienne comptable, une responsable RH et un conseiller juridique interne. Le président garde une seule chose : la relation avec les banques et les investisseurs. Tu prépares les chiffres, il porte la relation.

À qui ce poste convient

Au moins 10 ans en finance d'entreprise, idéalement multi-entités, en immobilier ou en construction ; CPA, un atout. Tu es rigoureux, tu respectes les processus et tu aides tout le monde à les respecter — président compris. Tu sais dire non avec calme. Tu tires ton énergie de mettre de l'ordre et de bâtir des systèmes qui tiennent sans toi.

À qui il conviendra moins

À quelqu'un qui pense en comptabilité plutôt qu'en cash, ou qui préfère attendre que les chiffres lui arrivent.

Ce que tu trouves ici

Un partage des profits : chaque tranche de 100 000 $ de profit net ajusté (après impôts, intérêts, comptes en retard et fonds de prévoyance) verse 10 000 $ au pool, divisé en parts égales entre tous les employés admissibles — dès le premier dollar, sans plafond
4 semaines de vacances
Un congé pour ton anniversaire et des congés mobiles
REER FTQ et assurances collectives
Le remboursement de ton cellulaire jusqu'à 80 $ par mois
Des bureaux modernes à Saint-Hubert, un club social, et ton chien est le bienvenu
La possibilité de devenir associé

Notre processus

Un appel découverte
Une rencontre avec le fondateur et le DG
Un vrai exercice : 13 semaines de flux de trésorerie de trois entités, avec un prêt entre elles — bâtir la prévision et nommer les trois plus grands risques
Une journée découverte avec l'équipe finance
Prise de références

Envoie ton CV et trois lignes sur la plus grosse mise en ordre financière que tu as menée.

At Vention, you’ll work alongside driven and talented people who care deeply about their craft and the impact they create. We’re a team of high achievers who grow through meaningful work, solving complex challenges, learning fast, and seeing the results of our efforts every day.

We move quickly and aim high, but we do it together with care, collaboration, and respect. Our culture celebrates diverse perspectives and supports your growth through intentional development, strong leadership, and opportunities to make a real difference.

What You’ll Do

Sitting at the nexus of robotics and Physical AI, Vention is transforming how businesses automate their factory floors. Scaling rapidly at Series D, Vention is on a fast track from hypergrowth scale-up to an IPO-ready enterprise. We are seeking a highly strategic but hands-on VP of Accounting to guide this transition and build a public company ready accounting function.

Public Readiness: Own and drive the roadmap to ensure Vention operates with public-company readiness within the next 24-36 months, supporting a potential IPO in the next 3 to 5 years. This will include an IFRS conversion and building a stronger internal controls framework
Team Development: Leading a team of 9 high performing professionals, you will cultivate a culture of accountability, operational excellence, and continuous professional development across the team
Controllership & Financial Close: Drive the monthly, quarterly, and year-end close cycles and lead the interim and annual cycles

Technical Accounting: Guide the preparation of technical accounting memos to support new business initiatives or transactions. Revenue recognition will be a particular focus, including addressing complex, multi-element revenue arrangements

Operational Finance: Optimize working capital through AR and AP management, streamline vendor disbursement cycles, enforce T&E policies, and ensure seamless payroll execution

12+ years of progressive accounting experience, with at least 4 years in a senior leadership role

You understand that successful clinics depend on effective operations, engaged people and accessible, patient-centred care. Masters Best Friend Inc. (MBF) is a Canadian-owned pet products company founded in Toronto, Ontario in 1993. For more than 30 years, we've focused on delivering high-quality products that support the health and wellbeing of dogs.

We're continuing to grow, and with that growth comes an opportunity to strengthen how we operate.
We're looking for a Director of Operations
to join our senior leadership team
and lead a critical part of our business across Ontario, British Columbia and Michigan
.

About the Role

This is not simply a warehouse-management role.

We're looking for an operational leader who can connect sales demand, inventory, procurement and production, ensuring we have the right products available at the right time while maintaining strong inventory controls and responsible working-capital management.

Equally important, this leader will develop a high-performing team and build a winning culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

The Director of Operations will have direct responsibility for inventory accuracy, production planning and scheduling, Bills of Materials (BOMs), warehousing, fulfillment and logistics across multiple locations.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The successful candidate will be comfortable working on the warehouse or production floor, developing their team, and using NetSuite, Excel and operational data to identify problems, understand root causes and drive better decisions.

What You'll Own

Inventory Accuracy & Control
Own inventory accuracy across raw materials, packaging, work in process and finished goods.
Establish and maintain strong inventory controls across receiving, transfers, production consumption, adjustments and shipping.
Lead effective cycle-counting and physical inventory programs across all locations.
Investigate differences between physical inventory and NetSuite and ensure discrepancies are resolved promptly.
Identify root causes of recurring inventory variances and implement sustainable corrective actions.
Monitor excess, obsolete, damaged and slow-moving inventory.
Partner closely with Finance on inventory reconciliation, valuation, reserves and audit requirements.

Product Availability & Procurement Planning
Work closely with Procurement to ensure sufficient raw materials, packaging and finished goods are available to support sales demand.
Translate sales forecasts, promotions and customer requirements into material and production requirements.
Monitor inventory, open purchase orders, supplier lead times, safety stock and expected demand to identify shortages before they affect customers or production.
Establish and maintain appropriate reorder points and safety-stock requirements.
Provide Procurement with clear visibility into what needs to be purchased and when.
Proactively identify supply or inventory risks and develop mitigation plans.
Balance product availability with inventory turns and responsible working-capital management.

Production Planning & Scheduling
Develop and maintain production schedules based on sales demand, required inventory, material availability, labour and production capacity.
Ensure raw materials and packaging are available before scheduled production begins.
Monitor actual production against schedule and address delays, material shortages and capacity constraints.
Coordinate production priorities across Operations, Procurement and Sales.
Monitor production yield, material usage, scrap, downtime and labour efficiency.
Ensure production consumption, completions and related inventory transactions are accurately and promptly recorded in NetSuite.
Identify production bottlenecks and implement practical improvements to increase capacity, reliability and productivity.

Bills of Materials
Build, maintain and continuously improve Bills of Materials (BOMs) for manufactured and assembled products.
Ensure BOMs accurately reflect raw materials, packaging, quantities, units of measure and expected production yields.
Maintain appropriate BOM approval, version-control and change processes.
Compare actual material consumption against BOM standards and investigate significant variances.
Ensure product and packaging changes are reflected in BOMs before production.
Partner with Finance, Procurement and Product teams to ensure BOM information supports accurate inventory costing and margin analysis.

Warehousing, Fulfillment & Logistics
Oversee receiving, storage, picking, packing, fulfillment and shipping operations.
Maintain effective warehouse layouts, inventory locations and material-flow processes.
Oversee transportation, cross-border logistics and inter-facility inventory transfers.
Monitor order accuracy, on-time shipment, freight costs and warehouse productivity.
Ensure appropriate inventory traceability and operational controls.
Identify opportunities to improve customer service while reducing operating and logistics costs.

Systems, Data & Analysis
Maintain strong operating discipline and data integrity in NetSuite and related systems.
Use advanced Excel skills to analyze inventory, demand, production requirements and operating performance.
Build practical analytical tools and reporting using capabilities such as PivotTables, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, Power Query and variance analysis.
Monitor key operating measures including inventory accuracy, stockouts, inventory turns and aging, production attainment, material usage, fulfillment performance and operational productivity.
Turn data into clear actions and use analysis to identify issues before they become problems.
Ensure operational reporting in Excel reconciles to NetSuite and other approved source systems.

Leadership & Team Development
Lead, coach and develop operations teams across multiple locations.
Build a high-performing team and a winning culture focused on accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Establish clear responsibilities, operating procedures and performance expectations.
Develop strong leaders within the operations organization and build appropriate cross-training and succession coverage.
Create an environment where team members understand how their work contributes to customers and overall business performance.
Promote strong standards for quality, safety, integrity and operational discipline.
Work collaboratively with Finance, Procurement, Sales, Product and other functions as a member of the MBF senior leadership team.

What We're Looking For
Significant experience in operations, inventory management, manufacturing, production planning, warehousing or supply chain, ideally in a multi-site environment.
Demonstrated success improving inventory accuracy and inventory-control processes.
Strong production planning and scheduling capabilities.
Hands-on experience creating and maintaining Bills of Materials (BOMs).
Strong understanding of inventory movements, material consumption, cycle counting and inventory reconciliation.
Strong Microsoft Excel skills and the ability to independently analyze large datasets and identify trends, exceptions and root causes.
Experience with ERP systems. Oracle NetSuite experience is strongly preferred.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capability combined with practical operational judgment.
Proven ability to build, lead and develop high-performing teams.
Ability to move comfortably between strategic planning, detailed data analysis and hands-on operational problem solving.
Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively across Finance, Procurement, Sales and other functions.
Experience operating in an environment where inventory availability, customer service and working capital must be carefully balanced.
Ability and willingness to travel regularly between St. Thomas, Ontario; Pitt Meadows, British Columbia; and Romeo, Michigan.

À propos de Pratt & Whitney Canada

Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.

Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.

Un employeur de choix

Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe?

Pratt & Whitney Canada est à la recherche d’un leader transformationnel pour occuper le poste de Directeur, PMO et excellence opérationnelle. Agissant comme le principal partenaire stratégique du directeur exécutif des technologies numériques, cette personne assurera une maîtrise rigoureuse, une visibilité complète et une exécution disciplinée de l’ensemble du portefeuille de projets numériques de P&WC. Il ne s’agit pas d’un rôle traditionnel de suivi de projets, mais d’un poste de leadership stratégique responsable de l’exécution, de la gouvernance, de la santé financière et de l’amélioration continue d’un portefeuille de transformation numérique de plusieurs millions de dollars.

En supervisant des initiatives complexes dans les domaines de l’ingénierie, de la fabrication, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des services après-vente et des fonctions corporatives, le directeur jouera un rôle de liaison essentiel entre P&WC, les organisations de livraison basées en Pologne et le PMO mondial de Pratt & Whitney. En intégrant la responsabilité financière et l’excellence opérationnelle au cadre de gestion du PMO, cette personne veillera à ce que les investissements technologiques stratégiques génèrent une valeur mesurable pour les résultats financiers et une transformation durable de l’entreprise.

Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil
, du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.

À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien?

Partenariat exécutif et gouvernance du portefeuille
Leadership opérationnel: Agir à titre de principal leader opérationnel des technologies numériques au Canada, en gérant les priorités concurrentes et en favorisant une étroite harmonisation entre les différentes unités d’affaires et régions géographiques.
Maturité du PMO: Définir et mettre en œuvre une stratégie pluriannuelle pour le PMO, en établissant des modèles opérationnels robustes, des cadres de gouvernance et des indicateurs de performance favorisant une exécution cohérente du portefeuille.
Stratégie d’investissement: Collaborer avec la direction pour identifier, prioriser et gérer l’allocation des fonds aux investissements technologiques stratégiques, tout en maintenant une feuille de route régionale de transformation numérique.
Visibilité exécutive: Mettre en place des tableaux de bord automatisés et des systèmes de gestion au sein de l’écosystème régional de gestion de portefeuille de projets (PPM), afin de fournir à la direction une visibilité en temps réel sur la santé du portefeuille, les risques et les résultats d’affaires.
Gestion et exécution de programmes complexes
Gestion de bout en bout: Diriger un portefeuille complexe de programmes de transformation à l’échelle de l’entreprise, en assurant la planification des ressources, la gestion des interdépendances interfonctionnelles et la résolution rapide des obstacles.
Envergure organisationnelle: Assurer la réalisation sans faille de programmes majeurs et essentiels aux activités de l’entreprise, notamment en matière de gestion du cycle de vie des produits (PLM), de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), de systèmes d’exécution de la fabrication (MES), de modernisation infonuagique et de plateformes de données et d’analytique.
Méthodologies de livraison: Promouvoir les meilleures pratiques en matière de méthodologies de gestion et de livraison de projets (Agile, SAFe, Waterfall et hybrides), et assurer l’application uniforme des pratiques de contrôle des projets et d’assurance qualité.
Excellence opérationnelle et réalisation de la valeur financière
Rigueur financière: Superviser la budgétisation, les prévisions et la gestion des investissements du portefeuille. Collaborer avec les équipes financières pour établir un suivi rigoureux du rendement des investissements (ROI), de la réalisation des bénéfices et des écarts.
Optimisation des processus: Harmoniser et optimiser les processus dans Planview afin d’éliminer les inefficacités, d’accélérer les délais de livraison et de surveiller les principaux indicateurs de santé opérationnelle.
Amélioration continue: Diriger des initiatives visant à améliorer la prévisibilité et à accélérer la mise en marché, en intégrant les principes du RTX Operating System à l’ensemble des activités d’exécution et d’amélioration du portefeuille.
Leadership du changement et développement des capacités organisationnelles
Développement des talents: Développer, encadrer et diriger une organisation PMO performante composée de gestionnaires de projets, de gestionnaires de programmes, de Scrum Masters et de leaders en transformation.
Intégration mondiale: Diriger la planification des ressources et l’optimisation des capacités entre les organisations de livraison au Canada et en Pologne, en comblant les lacunes en matière de compétences par le recours stratégique à des ressources externes et au recrutement.
Adoption par les utilisateurs: Assumer la responsabilité du cadre de gestion du changement pour les déploiements à grande échelle, en faisant évoluer l’approche du PMO au-delà de la mise en service (go-live) pour mettre l’accent sur l’adoption réelle par les utilisateurs et le succès après la mise en œuvre.
Gestion des parties prenantes: Établir des partenariats solides et fondés sur la confiance avec les équipes d’ingénierie, d’opérations, de chaîne d’approvisionnement, de MRO, de finances et de cybersécurité, afin d’assurer un soutien actif de la direction à l’ensemble des initiatives.
Gouvernance des risques et conformité à l’échelle de l’entreprise
Atténuation proactive: Diriger l’identification des risques systémiques liés au portefeuille, la planification des mesures d’atténuation et les processus d’escalade auprès de la direction afin de protéger les échéanciers stratégiques.
Conformité et audits: Veiller à ce que l’ensemble des cadres de livraison du PMO respecte rigoureusement les normes de conformité de l’industrie aérospatiale, les politiques corporatives, les exigences en matière de cybersécurité, les principes de gouvernance des données et les contrôles d’audit interne.

Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une très bonne connaissance de l’anglais pour lire et comprendre, sur une base quotidienne, de la documentation et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales, ainsi que pour écrire et communiquer en anglais avec des clients, des fournisseurs ou des collègues internationaux.

Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir?

Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en génie, en administration des affaires, en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe.
Plus de 14 ans d’expérience progressive en technologies numériques, en gestion de programmes, en leadership PMO ou en transformation organisationnelle.
Expérience approfondie dans la direction de portefeuilles de projets d’envergure, la gestion de budgets de plusieurs millions de dollars et la réalisation de programmes de transformation numérique.
Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place et la gestion de PMO au sein de l’industrie aérospatiale, de l’aviation, de la fabrication de pointe ou d’autres secteurs complexes et fortement réglementés.
Excellentes aptitudes en leadership exécutif et capacité éprouvée à influencer les dirigeants, à résoudre les conflits et à favoriser le consensus au sein d’organisations matricielles réparties géographiquement.
Certification PMP (Project Management Professional).
Certification PgMP (Program Management Professional) et/ou PfMP (Portfolio Management Professional).
Certification SAFe Program Consultant (SPC) ou SAFe Agilist.
Certifications en gestion de projets Agile.
Certification Lean Six Sigma.

Qualifications Privilégiées

Maîtrise en administration des affaires (MBA), en systèmes d’information, en génie ou dans un domaine connexe.
Expérience approfondie dans le soutien aux initiatives de transformation en ingénierie, en fabrication, en chaîne d’approvisionnement et dans les services après-vente.
Expérience démontrée dans des modèles de livraison mondiaux et dans la gestion de relations avec des fournisseurs et partenaires multinationaux.
Bonne connaissance pratique des méthodologies RTX Operating System, des concepts d’architecture d’entreprise et des principes de gouvernance des données.

Executive Council works to ensure effective strategic planning and coordinated policy development and communications across government, engages Albertans and the broader global community, and promotes a vibrant and innovative public service. In addition to policy, protocol, communications and Cabinet functions, Executive Council includes Communications and Public Engagement (CPE). CPE is the Government of Alberta's full-service communications, public relations and marketing department. Its mandate is to enhance communications between Albertans and the Government of Alberta.

CPE’s expert staff provide specialized services across the spectrum of communications including writing, social media, media relations, event coordination, issues management, crisis communications, digital communications, advertising, marketing, graphic design, public engagement and translation services. Behind strong communications decisions is a clear understanding of what is happening, what the evidence is telling us and where attention is needed next.

As the Assistant Director, Communications Planning and Analysis, you will lead the team that turns communications data, research and intelligence into actionable insights. From emerging media trends and public sentiment to performance results and environmental scans, you will help senior leaders understand the communications landscape and use evidence to inform planning and decision-making.

This role brings together communications strategy, analytics and leadership. You will lead communications measurement and evaluation, executive reporting and strategic analysis, while strengthening consistent approaches to planning and reporting across government. You will also champion new ways of working, including the effective use of technology, automation and artificial intelligence.

In This Role, You Will

Strategic Communications Intelligence & Executive Advice

Identify emerging issues, risks and opportunities and translate complex information into actionable executive advice.
Direct executive briefings, dashboards and strategic assessments that support timely, evidence-based decision-making.

Performance Measurement & Evaluation

Lead communications measurement and evaluation frameworks, including key performance indicators and outcomes.

Leadership & Communications Planning

Cross-Government Coordination & Continuous Improvement

Advance modern approaches to analysis and reporting, including technology, automation and artificial intelligence.
Strengthen reporting tools, analytical practices, information governance and quality assurance.

You consider the broader communications environment and understand how emerging issues, trends, government priorities and organizational decisions connect and influence one another.

Own HR modernization delivery: Translate enterprise and HR strategy into an integrated modernization agenda that delivers simpler colleague experiences, greater productivity and measurable business value.

You will manage a dedicated team of risk professionals and act as a senior expert advisor across the second line of defense. Strategic Leadership & Governance

Develop and execute the long-term vision, strategy, and operating standards for the Trade Floor Market Risk Oversight and Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR) pillars.
Own, maintain, and spearhead limit reviews and calibrations, collaborating with risk and front office stakeholders to ensure risk limits are aligned with risk appetite and business strategy.
Be the subject matter expert for annual and intra-cycle updates of the Board-level Market Risk Management Policy and accompanying Frameworks.
Act as a core member and senior presenter at the Market Risk Oversight Committee (MROC), presenting key market and counterparty credit risk insights and effectively escalating risk postures to the Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO).
Lead the review and implementation of new traded products via the New Initiative Risk Assessment Process (NIRAP) to safely onboard new capital market instruments and product lines.
Design, implement, and execute a rigorous 2nd line control framework to continuously validate market risk and counterparty credit risk models via systematic backtesting.

Market Risk Oversight & Analytics

Oversee independent daily monitoring and granular analysis of desk-level trading risks across traded securities and derivatives products (including Fixed Income, Interest Rates, Foreign Exchange, Equities, and Commodities).
Ensure absolute integrity of end-of-day (EOD) and intra-day risk reporting metrics, including Value-at-Risk (VaR), Stressed VaR (SVaR), sensitivities/Greeks (DV01, CS01), and Notional limits.
Direct real-time limit excess management and breach escalation protocols across first and second lines of defense.
Drive the end-to-end framework for ensuring that market risk models, measurements, and risk engines are structurally sound, comprehensive, and accurate.
Establish robust processes and controls to guarantee that all risk factors—specifically complex nuances like basis risk (including tenor, currency, and index basis mismatches), volatility smiles, and correlation breakdowns—are fully captured, mapped, and measured
Lead the development and enhancement of trade floor and counterparty credit risk reporting and analytics to foster proactive risk management.
Strengthen and maintain the robustness of market risk frameworks by effectively identifying and capturing risks across unique, complex, and bespoke business lines (e.g., equity bought deals, off-market trades)

Ensure the completeness, accuracy, and rigorous governance of model inputs feeding into counterparty credit risk engines, including credit curve mappings, ensuring that Potential Future Exposure (PFE) model parameters are mathematically sound and reflective of current market dynamics

Strengthen Counterparty Credit Risk policies & frameworks by aligning with industry and regulatory best practices.

Mastered expertise in multi-asset Capital Markets financial instruments (FICC derivatives, equities, repo, debt capital markets).
Advanced understanding of derivative pricing, risk-neutral and real-world simulation modeling frameworks, Monte Carlo engines, and volatility skews/smiles.
In-depth practical knowledge of risk systems, specifically Murex and Bloomberg (MARS/TOMS).
Quantitative data proficiency utilizing tools like Python, SQL, and Google BigQuery (DEEP architecture).

Proven people leader capable of mentoring high-performing analysts and managers, cultivating technical excellence, and fostering a collaborative, psychological safe culture.

In your new role as a Director, AI Governance & Enablement, you will be accountable for operating and advancing company’s enterprise AI practice. It is not a research or data science role.

You will operate the governance processes that determine how AI is introduced into day-to-day work, help departments identify and prioritize valuable AI use cases, and ensure AI systems are deployed responsibly as they become more multimodal, more connected to enterprise data, and more capable of influencing decisions, workflows, and user behaviour. The role also serves as AI expertise-as-a-service function, working across corporate departments, FASTech, Service Management & Automation, Business Analysis & Quality Assurance, Data & Analytics, Privacy, Cybersecurity, and enterprise applications so that AI-enabled solutions are useful, explainable, governable, and aligned to operational realities.

The position has no direct reports. Authority is exercised through ownership of enterprise AI governance processes, leadership of the AI enablement program portfolio, management of third-party AI partner relationships, and cross-functional influence rather than direct supervision. The role owns the working relationship with external AI platform providers, training partners, and advisory firms — holding them to company’s governance, privacy, and security expectations, and leveraging them to extend internal AI education and enablement capacity. Governance framework design, risk-tier definitions, and final approval authority for higher-risk AI initiatives rest with the Director, Innovation & Technology Enablement; this role recommends, operates, and enforces.

Key Accountabilities

Enterprise AI Governance

Recommend, maintain, and continuously improve AI governance framework, standards, guardrails, and acceptable-use practices in alignment with legal, privacy, security, and risk requirements, escalating framework changes to the Director for approval.
Apply and document practical controls for responsible AI use, including human accountability, override mechanisms, confidence thresholds, auditability, data handling expectations, and documentation standards.
Operate the AI intake and review process end to end — triage, assessment, and recommendation on appropriateness, value, risk, explainability, and organizational readiness.
Apply established risk classification and approval paths, distinguishing between low-risk productivity uses, operational decision support, and higher-risk use cases, and route initiatives above the defined threshold to the Director for decision.
Partner with Privacy, Cybersecurity, Legal, and enterprise technology leaders to ensure AI-enabled solutions meet policy, compliance, and audit expectations.
Define and apply governance expectations for third-party AI providers and partners, including data handling, model transparency, sub-processor disclosure, and alignment to company’s privacy and security requirements, working with Privacy, Cybersecurity, Legal, and Procurement.

Create and maintain practical playbooks, templates, examples, and decision guides that help teams use AI effectively and responsibly.
Promote AI literacy across the organization by translating technical concepts into plain-language guidance and actionable practices.
Support leaders in understanding the opportunities and risks of multimodal AI, connected AI, agentic workflows, and AI-assisted decision support.
Track adoption, usage patterns, and learning outcomes to refine enablement programs and improve organizational readiness.

Help teams convert ambiguous problems into clear AI and automation use cases with defined objectives, constraints, risks, and success measures.

Act as a trusted internal partner who helps departments move from experimentation to controlled, business-aligned AI adoption.

Role Summary

The Director, Non-Financial Risk Assessment Programs leads how Capital Markets carries out BMO's main non-financial risk identification and assessment programs: PRC (Process, Risk & Control) and Risk ID inventories and RCSA (Risk & Control Self-Assessment) and RCRAs (Regulatory Compliance Risk Assessment). They make sure assessments are accurate, defensible, delivered on time, and meet ONFR and ECP requirements.

The Director brings a deep understanding of how risks, controls, processes, products, business units and legal entities connect across Capital Markets. They advocate with enterprise program owners for structures and methodologies that fit the business. The role improves inventory quality, makes execution consistent across business units (BUs), reduces the workload on Business Controls and Business Units and improves portfolio level assessments

Key Accountabilities

Inventory governance and PRC management
Own year-round governance and data-quality oversight of BU PRC inventories (products and services, internal activities, processes, specific risks and controls).
Lead the annual PRC Inventory Confirmation.
Manage organizational and ownership changes, including BU realignments, lift-and-shifts, new inventory builds, MCC/ME updates and inventory rationalization.
Monitor inventory health through Risk Mart and Power BI. Find missing attributes, linkages and data-quality issues, then drive remediation and escalate unresolved gaps.
Make sure applicable Master Common Controls (MCCs) and shared controls are adopted correctly in BU control inventories, including SOX designations.
Capital Markets risk structure and cross-program linkages
Act as the authoritative interpreter of PRC, RCSA, RCRA for Capital Markets.
Act as Capital Markets' expert on how products and services, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities connect, and keep that view current as the business and organization change.
Advocate with the enterprise program owner for the data structure, taxonomy and linkage design that best fits Capital Markets, including how KRIs, Issues and Events connect to PRC risk and control records.
Give business requirements and practical input on changes to the GRCE data model, workflow and future-state integration, including aggregation at the Legal Entity level.
Make sure Capital Markets inventories apply the agreed linkage standards consistently. This includes keeping Issues linked to Key Controls complete and accurate
Find structural gaps or misalignments, such as missing, orphaned or inconsistent linkages, and bring them to the program owner with recommended fixes.
Use the linked data to support RCSA residual risk ratings, overrides and Targeted Risk Evaluations (TREs) with evidence, and to show where control weaknesses, KRI breaches and loss events cluster.
Risk assessment execution (RCSA and RCRA)
Lead the PRC/RCSA/RCRA Annual Plan.
Oversee risk categorization (key vs. non-key) and ensure assessments are right sized taking a risk based approach.
Oversee reviews of TREs, including inherent risk, control effectiveness, residual risk, overrides and rationales. Ensure High Residual Risk ratings have corrective actions to improve control effectiveness.

Produce AE summary materials and approval packages, and keep approval evidence in GRCE.
Provide risk profile insights and committee reporting (for example, VRC).

Lead improvements to methodology, process, reporting and systems with ONFR. Standardize tools, templates and procedures.
Represent Capital Markets in working groups, user acceptance testing (UAT) and platform evaluations to shape GRCE and future assessment capabilities.
People leadership
Lead, develop and set priorities for team members and Business Control teams across concurrent assessment cycles.
Build a culture of accountability, data quality and practical, business-friendly risk partnership.

Key relationships

1LOD: Business Controls, Risk Domain Leads, Business Unit Leads, Accountable Executives, Operational Resilience & Risk Programs, Portfolio Analytics, Capital Markets Assurance Role, Enterprise Control Functions
2LOD: ONFR and ECP program & methodology owners, OROs, RSAs, Regulatory Compliance and Privacy

Qualifications

10+ years in operational or non-financial risk, risk and control self-assessment, or governance at a large financial institution, including people leadership. Capital Markets experience strongly preferred.
Deep understanding of how Capital Markets products, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities relate, and the ability to turn that into clear structural requirements for enterprise program owners.
Deep knowledge of the three lines of defence model, risk and control taxonomies, residual risk methods and Effective Challenge.
Proven ability to influence and negotiate with 2LOD and enterprise program owners, representing business interests credibly and constructively.
Hands-on experience with a GRC platform (Archer preferred) and with data and reporting tools (Power BI, Risk Mart).
Track record of leading enterprise programs on regulatory deadlines and producing audit- ready, AE-ready and committee-ready materials.
Strong judgment and executive presence, and the ability to escalate issues diplomatically with senior stakeholders.

Come join an organization committed to delivering innovative solutions.

They understand the business strategy, the unit’s enterprise architecture strategy and translate both into system changes required for achievement.

This role collaborates with the Enterprise Architect and Infrastructure and Operations leaders on the development of the Infrastructure and Operations IT Strategy. The successful candidate will provide technology leadership and innovation focused on the Hosting Services Portfolio. The Hosting Services Portfolio Architect is responsible for governing the technology architecture across Public Cloud providers and on-premises data centres for the following services:

Compute Services: Virtual Compute, Containers, Physical Compute, Mainframe
Storage Services: Networked Storage, File & Object Storage, Data Protection
Monitoring and Observability Services: IT Infrastructure Management, Network Performance Monitoring and Diagnostics, Application Performance Management, and AI for Operations.

Accountable to ensure high-quality delivery of leading-edge solutions that meet time and cost requirements that align with Infrastructure and Operations and Enterprise Architecture principles and design standards.
Enable Infrastructure and Operations portfolio goals through the construction of IT strategies, technology roadmaps, architectural standards and patterns to achieve business plans.
Guide Solutions Architects in developing designs that align with portfolio architecture directions and balance the realities of funding, time and delivery.
Provide consultative advice to business leaders and organizational stakeholders who seek actionable recommendations to make investment decisions using technology to enable change.
Research and recommend opportunities to leverage technology and keep up with the industry to support the strategy.
Provide leadership in managing IT risk (e.g.: security, resiliency, technology solution quality, etc.) and control requirements.
Ensure leaders, employees and vendors work together to drive performance and that high expectations are achieved within the values of the organization.
Apply knowledge, experience and new ways of thinking about issues to resolve complex & unusual problems facing the portfolio.
