Bachelor Computer Science / Software Engineering or equivalent degree/experience.
10+ years of experience in IT environments with a preference for significant complexity, highly regulated, and/or financial services.
5+ progressive leadership experience related to both projects and teams.
Prior experience working in an Architect capacity and exposure to Architecture governance and thought leadership in Hosting Services architecture.
Extensive experience with virtualization, compute, storage and data protection technologies and services.
Expertise with Kubernetes, container platforms, and modern workload hosting environments.
Experience with technologies, services and approaches for observability that focus on the end-to-end experience enabling higher reliability, faster incident response and improved customer experience.
Expertise in both Cloud and on-premises Hosting Services architecture with a preference for Cloud Hosting Services experience over traditional on-premises hosting.
Exceptional documentation skills, with a proven history of developing and maintaining architecture artifacts including capability maps, reference architectures, standards, roadmaps, architecture decision records, and executive presentations.

Manage strategic application vendors and implementation partners.
Build internal application capability while reducing key-person and vendor dependency.
Ensure critical applications are reliable, secure, supportable and scalable.

10+ years of progressive enterprise applications or technology experience.
5+ years leading application, ERP or digital-transformation teams.
Proven experience with ERP modernization and business-process transformation.
Experience managing complex enterprise application portfolios and vendors.
Strong understanding of ERP, integrations, APIs, application lifecycle management and IT service management.
Experience in aviation, aerospace, defense, MRO, manufacturing or another asset-intensive environment is highly desirable.
Experience with Ramco Aviation/MRO is a strong asset.
Strong business and executive communication skills.
Bachelor's degree in Technology, Engineering, Business or a related discipline.

What Success Looks Like

Top Aces moves from fragmented applications and manual workarounds toward a simplified, integrated and resilient enterprise application ecosystem that improves mission readiness, operational efficiency and global scalability.

Why Top Aces

This is an opportunity to shape the enterprise application landscape of a growing global aerospace and defense organization. You will influence major technology and business-process decisions and build an Enterprise Applications capability designed for the company's next stage of growth.

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

The Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) team is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technologies and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada, but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

Role Vision and Impact

The Senior Director, Information Security and End-User Technology, serves as CBC/Radio-Canada’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). A strategic, visionary and collaborative leader, the CISO defines, implements and drives the overarching vision for cybersecurity, risk management and technological resilience across all corporate environments.

The mission of this strategic role is to protect information assets, data, digital heritage, and production and broadcasting infrastructure across all platforms, while ensuring seamless, agile and uninterrupted media operations.
The Senior Director optimally balances rigorous security architecture governance with the flexibility that creative, journalistic and technical teams need to innovate and broadcast without disruption.

Operating at a senior executive level, the CISO regularly briefs and advises the Board of Directors (BoD),
the Audit Committee,
the CBC/Radio-Canada Senior Executive Team (SET)
and the T&I Management Executive Team (MET).

Supported by a team of experienced directors and senior managers overseeing governance, security operations, end-user technology and identity management, the Senior Director serves as the cornerstone of digital trust and strategic transformation for Canada’s public broadcaster.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Vision, Leadership and Executive Relations

Develop, champion and execute an enterprise-wide cybersecurity strategy aligned with the Corporation’s business mission, risk profile and digital transformation.
Serve as a trusted expert and strategic adviser to the BoD, Audit Committee, SET and MET regarding risk status, security posture and maturity, and required investments.
Foster a “Security by Design” culture and establish security architecture governance frameworks that keep operational and production workflows running smoothly while proactively managing risk.
Anticipate technology trends and lead the secure integration of artificial intelligence (AI/GenAI) and automation into business processes and security defences across the organization.

Securing IT, Cloud, Distribution and Broadcast/Operational Technology (OT) Environments

Define and continuously adapt the security strategy across the entire technology landscape, including corporate IT infrastructure, cloud systems, end-user environments, and critical production, broadcast and network infrastructure.
Ensure the resilience of content acquisition, processing and distribution workflows against threats targeting the media sector and critical infrastructure.

Governance, Risk, Compliance and AI Governance

Oversee the governance function responsible for developing, maintaining and enforcing policies, standards, security architecture principles, exception management and industry frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, AI frameworks).
Lead the third-party and partner risk management program (covering vendors and technology contracts) in close collaboration with the Legal Services and Procurement teams.
Co-develop a governance, compliance and ethical framework for the enterprise-wide use of AI and generative AI, assessing specific risks throughout their life cycle.
Ensure strict compliance with applicable laws and regulations (e.g., Quebec’s Law 25, GDPR and sector-specific requirements).
Drive a cybersecurity culture and awareness program focused on lasting behaviour change across the organization.

Defence Operations, SOC and Crisis Management

Oversee the performance and modernization of the Security Operations Centre (SOC), advanced detection tools (SIEM, EDR/XDR, automation) and continuous threat monitoring.
Direct major security incident response operations and lead technology crisis management, from detection to full business recovery.
Oversee regular penetration testing, vulnerability assessments and cyberattack simulation exercises across IT, broadcast and distribution environments.

Identity and End-User Technology

Guide the strategic vision for Identity and Access Management (IAM, PAM) to provide secure, simple and frictionless access for all staff and contractors.
Collaborate closely with the End-User Technology teams to align security with a modern, efficient and intuitive employee experience.

Financial Management and Team Engagement

Plan and optimize the cybersecurity department’s overall budget and partner with internal procurement teams to negotiate major technology contracts.
Inspire, coach and develop a team of directors and senior managers — fostering excellence, innovation and cross-functional collaboration.
Lead with the heart.

At least one recognized executive-level professional certification: CISSP, CISM, CCISO, CISA or CRISC.

Professional Experience

Deep expertise in technology architecture, cloud security, network infrastructure, cryptography, and identity and access management (IAM).
Ability to provide collaborative leadership within the organization to see complex, transformational initiatives through to completion.
Demonstrated skills in planning, organizing and engaging teams.
Proven ability and track record in leading cross-functional teams.
Proven ability to work with cross-functional, agile teams or on projects that have multi-team dependencies.
Ability to distil complex issues into clear, concise presentations and reports.

Knowledge of business practices, including drafting plans and specifications, contracts, negotiation, finance, and IT management software.
Knowledge of software development and the technology infrastructure required for product delivery.
Knowledge of workflows for content acquisition, management and distribution, with a focus on storytelling.
Innovative approach to technical and operational challenges, paired with sound judgment to protect CBC/Radio-Canada from legal liability and financial loss.
Excellent interpersonal skills, with an ability to engage and influence stakeholders and partners at every level of the organization.
Excellent ability to listen to and communicate with people having different points of view or competing business objectives.

Expert-comptable agréé (CPA) en exercice, avec de l'expérience au sein d'un cabinet du Big Four et une expertise en normes IFRS.

Masters Best Friend Inc. (MBF) is a Canadian-owned pet products company founded in Toronto, Ontario in 1993. For more than 30 years, we've focused on delivering high-quality products that support the health and wellbeing of dogs.

We're continuing to grow, and with that growth comes an opportunity to strengthen how we operate.
We're looking for a Director of Operations
to join our senior leadership team
and lead a critical part of our business across Ontario, British Columbia and Michigan
.

About the Role

This is not simply a warehouse-management role.

We're looking for an operational leader who can connect sales demand, inventory, procurement and production, ensuring we have the right products available at the right time while maintaining strong inventory controls and responsible working-capital management.

Equally important, this leader will develop a high-performing team and build a winning culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

The Director of Operations will have direct responsibility for inventory accuracy, production planning and scheduling, Bills of Materials (BOMs), warehousing, fulfillment and logistics across multiple locations.

This is a hands-on leadership role. The successful candidate will be comfortable working on the warehouse or production floor, developing their team, and using NetSuite, Excel and operational data to identify problems, understand root causes and drive better decisions.

What You'll Own

Inventory Accuracy & Control
Own inventory accuracy across raw materials, packaging, work in process and finished goods.
Establish and maintain strong inventory controls across receiving, transfers, production consumption, adjustments and shipping.
Lead effective cycle-counting and physical inventory programs across all locations.
Investigate differences between physical inventory and NetSuite and ensure discrepancies are resolved promptly.
Identify root causes of recurring inventory variances and implement sustainable corrective actions.
Monitor excess, obsolete, damaged and slow-moving inventory.
Partner closely with Finance on inventory reconciliation, valuation, reserves and audit requirements.

Product Availability & Procurement Planning
Work closely with Procurement to ensure sufficient raw materials, packaging and finished goods are available to support sales demand.
Translate sales forecasts, promotions and customer requirements into material and production requirements.
Monitor inventory, open purchase orders, supplier lead times, safety stock and expected demand to identify shortages before they affect customers or production.
Establish and maintain appropriate reorder points and safety-stock requirements.
Provide Procurement with clear visibility into what needs to be purchased and when.
Proactively identify supply or inventory risks and develop mitigation plans.
Balance product availability with inventory turns and responsible working-capital management.

Production Planning & Scheduling
Develop and maintain production schedules based on sales demand, required inventory, material availability, labour and production capacity.
Ensure raw materials and packaging are available before scheduled production begins.
Monitor actual production against schedule and address delays, material shortages and capacity constraints.
Coordinate production priorities across Operations, Procurement and Sales.
Monitor production yield, material usage, scrap, downtime and labour efficiency.
Ensure production consumption, completions and related inventory transactions are accurately and promptly recorded in NetSuite.
Identify production bottlenecks and implement practical improvements to increase capacity, reliability and productivity.

Bills of Materials
Build, maintain and continuously improve Bills of Materials (BOMs) for manufactured and assembled products.
Ensure BOMs accurately reflect raw materials, packaging, quantities, units of measure and expected production yields.
Maintain appropriate BOM approval, version-control and change processes.
Compare actual material consumption against BOM standards and investigate significant variances.
Ensure product and packaging changes are reflected in BOMs before production.
Partner with Finance, Procurement and Product teams to ensure BOM information supports accurate inventory costing and margin analysis.

Warehousing, Fulfillment & Logistics
Oversee receiving, storage, picking, packing, fulfillment and shipping operations.
Maintain effective warehouse layouts, inventory locations and material-flow processes.
Oversee transportation, cross-border logistics and inter-facility inventory transfers.
Monitor order accuracy, on-time shipment, freight costs and warehouse productivity.
Ensure appropriate inventory traceability and operational controls.
Identify opportunities to improve customer service while reducing operating and logistics costs.

Systems, Data & Analysis
Maintain strong operating discipline and data integrity in NetSuite and related systems.
Use advanced Excel skills to analyze inventory, demand, production requirements and operating performance.
Build practical analytical tools and reporting using capabilities such as PivotTables, XLOOKUP, SUMIFS, Power Query and variance analysis.
Monitor key operating measures including inventory accuracy, stockouts, inventory turns and aging, production attainment, material usage, fulfillment performance and operational productivity.
Turn data into clear actions and use analysis to identify issues before they become problems.
Ensure operational reporting in Excel reconciles to NetSuite and other approved source systems.

Leadership & Team Development
Lead, coach and develop operations teams across multiple locations.
Build a high-performing team and a winning culture focused on accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Establish clear responsibilities, operating procedures and performance expectations.
Develop strong leaders within the operations organization and build appropriate cross-training and succession coverage.
Create an environment where team members understand how their work contributes to customers and overall business performance.
Promote strong standards for quality, safety, integrity and operational discipline.
Work collaboratively with Finance, Procurement, Sales, Product and other functions as a member of the MBF senior leadership team.

Significant experience in operations, inventory management, manufacturing, production planning, warehousing or supply chain, ideally in a multi-site environment.
Demonstrated success improving inventory accuracy and inventory-control processes.
Strong production planning and scheduling capabilities.
Hands-on experience creating and maintaining Bills of Materials (BOMs).
Strong understanding of inventory movements, material consumption, cycle counting and inventory reconciliation.
Strong Microsoft Excel skills and the ability to independently analyze large datasets and identify trends, exceptions and root causes.

Strong analytical and problem-solving capability combined with practical operational judgment.

Strong communication skills and the ability to work effectively across Finance, Procurement, Sales and other functions.
Experience operating in an environment where inventory availability, customer service and working capital must be carefully balanced.
Ability and willingness to travel regularly between St. Thomas, Ontario; Pitt Meadows, British Columbia; and Romeo, Michigan.

L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.

Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe?

Pratt & Whitney Canada est à la recherche d’un leader transformationnel pour occuper le poste de Directeur, PMO et excellence opérationnelle. Agissant comme le principal partenaire stratégique du directeur exécutif des technologies numériques, cette personne assurera une maîtrise rigoureuse, une visibilité complète et une exécution disciplinée de l’ensemble du portefeuille de projets numériques de P&WC. Il ne s’agit pas d’un rôle traditionnel de suivi de projets, mais d’un poste de leadership stratégique responsable de l’exécution, de la gouvernance, de la santé financière et de l’amélioration continue d’un portefeuille de transformation numérique de plusieurs millions de dollars.

En supervisant des initiatives complexes dans les domaines de l’ingénierie, de la fabrication, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des services après-vente et des fonctions corporatives, le directeur jouera un rôle de liaison essentiel entre P&WC, les organisations de livraison basées en Pologne et le PMO mondial de Pratt & Whitney. En intégrant la responsabilité financière et l’excellence opérationnelle au cadre de gestion du PMO, cette personne veillera à ce que les investissements technologiques stratégiques génèrent une valeur mesurable pour les résultats financiers et une transformation durable de l’entreprise.

Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil
, du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.

À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien?

Partenariat exécutif et gouvernance du portefeuille
Leadership opérationnel: Agir à titre de principal leader opérationnel des technologies numériques au Canada, en gérant les priorités concurrentes et en favorisant une étroite harmonisation entre les différentes unités d’affaires et régions géographiques.
Maturité du PMO: Définir et mettre en œuvre une stratégie pluriannuelle pour le PMO, en établissant des modèles opérationnels robustes, des cadres de gouvernance et des indicateurs de performance favorisant une exécution cohérente du portefeuille.
Stratégie d’investissement: Collaborer avec la direction pour identifier, prioriser et gérer l’allocation des fonds aux investissements technologiques stratégiques, tout en maintenant une feuille de route régionale de transformation numérique.
Visibilité exécutive: Mettre en place des tableaux de bord automatisés et des systèmes de gestion au sein de l’écosystème régional de gestion de portefeuille de projets (PPM), afin de fournir à la direction une visibilité en temps réel sur la santé du portefeuille, les risques et les résultats d’affaires.
Gestion et exécution de programmes complexes
Gestion de bout en bout: Diriger un portefeuille complexe de programmes de transformation à l’échelle de l’entreprise, en assurant la planification des ressources, la gestion des interdépendances interfonctionnelles et la résolution rapide des obstacles.
Envergure organisationnelle: Assurer la réalisation sans faille de programmes majeurs et essentiels aux activités de l’entreprise, notamment en matière de gestion du cycle de vie des produits (PLM), de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), de systèmes d’exécution de la fabrication (MES), de modernisation infonuagique et de plateformes de données et d’analytique.
Méthodologies de livraison: Promouvoir les meilleures pratiques en matière de méthodologies de gestion et de livraison de projets (Agile, SAFe, Waterfall et hybrides), et assurer l’application uniforme des pratiques de contrôle des projets et d’assurance qualité.
Excellence opérationnelle et réalisation de la valeur financière
Rigueur financière: Superviser la budgétisation, les prévisions et la gestion des investissements du portefeuille. Collaborer avec les équipes financières pour établir un suivi rigoureux du rendement des investissements (ROI), de la réalisation des bénéfices et des écarts.
Optimisation des processus: Harmoniser et optimiser les processus dans Planview afin d’éliminer les inefficacités, d’accélérer les délais de livraison et de surveiller les principaux indicateurs de santé opérationnelle.
Amélioration continue: Diriger des initiatives visant à améliorer la prévisibilité et à accélérer la mise en marché, en intégrant les principes du RTX Operating System à l’ensemble des activités d’exécution et d’amélioration du portefeuille.
Leadership du changement et développement des capacités organisationnelles
Développement des talents: Développer, encadrer et diriger une organisation PMO performante composée de gestionnaires de projets, de gestionnaires de programmes, de Scrum Masters et de leaders en transformation.
Intégration mondiale: Diriger la planification des ressources et l’optimisation des capacités entre les organisations de livraison au Canada et en Pologne, en comblant les lacunes en matière de compétences par le recours stratégique à des ressources externes et au recrutement.
Adoption par les utilisateurs: Assumer la responsabilité du cadre de gestion du changement pour les déploiements à grande échelle, en faisant évoluer l’approche du PMO au-delà de la mise en service (go-live) pour mettre l’accent sur l’adoption réelle par les utilisateurs et le succès après la mise en œuvre.
Gestion des parties prenantes: Établir des partenariats solides et fondés sur la confiance avec les équipes d’ingénierie, d’opérations, de chaîne d’approvisionnement, de MRO, de finances et de cybersécurité, afin d’assurer un soutien actif de la direction à l’ensemble des initiatives.
Gouvernance des risques et conformité à l’échelle de l’entreprise
Atténuation proactive: Diriger l’identification des risques systémiques liés au portefeuille, la planification des mesures d’atténuation et les processus d’escalade auprès de la direction afin de protéger les échéanciers stratégiques.
Conformité et audits: Veiller à ce que l’ensemble des cadres de livraison du PMO respecte rigoureusement les normes de conformité de l’industrie aérospatiale, les politiques corporatives, les exigences en matière de cybersécurité, les principes de gouvernance des données et les contrôles d’audit interne.

Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une très bonne connaissance de l’anglais pour lire et comprendre, sur une base quotidienne, de la documentation et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales, ainsi que pour écrire et communiquer en anglais avec des clients, des fournisseurs ou des collègues internationaux.

Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir?

Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en génie, en administration des affaires, en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe.
Plus de 14 ans d’expérience progressive en technologies numériques, en gestion de programmes, en leadership PMO ou en transformation organisationnelle.

Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place et la gestion de PMO au sein de l’industrie aérospatiale, de l’aviation, de la fabrication de pointe ou d’autres secteurs complexes et fortement réglementés.
Excellentes aptitudes en leadership exécutif et capacité éprouvée à influencer les dirigeants, à résoudre les conflits et à favoriser le consensus au sein d’organisations matricielles réparties géographiquement.

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding career opportunities.

Executive Council works to ensure effective strategic planning and coordinated policy development and communications across government, engages Albertans and the broader global community, and promotes a vibrant and innovative public service. In addition to policy, protocol, communications and Cabinet functions, Executive Council includes Communications and Public Engagement (CPE). CPE is the Government of Alberta's full-service communications, public relations and marketing department. Its mandate is to enhance communications between Albertans and the Government of Alberta.

CPE’s expert staff provide specialized services across the spectrum of communications including writing, social media, media relations, event coordination, issues management, crisis communications, digital communications, advertising, marketing, graphic design, public engagement and translation services. The department staffs the communications branches in all ministries of government, and provides centralized research, engagement, advertising and media services to government.

Role Responsibilities

Behind strong communications decisions is a clear understanding of what is happening, what the evidence is telling us and where attention is needed next.

As the Assistant Director, Communications Planning and Analysis, you will lead the team that turns communications data, research and intelligence into actionable insights. From emerging media trends and public sentiment to performance results and environmental scans, you will help senior leaders understand the communications landscape and use evidence to inform planning and decision-making.

This role brings together communications strategy, analytics and leadership. You will lead communications measurement and evaluation, executive reporting and strategic analysis, while strengthening consistent approaches to planning and reporting across government. You will also champion new ways of working, including the effective use of technology, automation and artificial intelligence.

In This Role, You Will

Strategic Communications Intelligence & Executive Advice

Lead environmental scanning, media and public sentiment analysis, stakeholder intelligence and trend identification.
Identify emerging issues, risks and opportunities and translate complex information into actionable executive advice.
Direct executive briefings, dashboards and strategic assessments that support timely, evidence-based decision-making.

Performance Measurement & Evaluation

Lead communications measurement and evaluation frameworks, including key performance indicators and outcomes.
Translate performance data and evaluation findings into insights that strengthen communications effectiveness and inform continuous improvement.

Leadership & Communications Planning

Lead the Communications Planning and Analysis function, setting priorities and aligning work with divisional, ministry and Government of Alberta objectives.
Develop and support staff while fostering collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.

Cross-Government Coordination & Continuous Improvement

Build collaborative relationships across government to strengthen communications planning, intelligence, measurement and reporting.
Advance modern approaches to analysis and reporting, including technology, automation and artificial intelligence.
Strengthen reporting tools, analytical practices, information governance and quality assurance.

The Job Description
is provided for further details on this position.

APS Competencies

Competencies are behaviors that are essential to reach our goals in serving Albertans. We encourage you to have an in-depth understanding of the competencies that are required for this opportunity and to be prepared to demonstrate them during the recruitment process.

Systems Thinking:
You consider the broader communications environment and understand how emerging issues, trends, government priorities and organizational decisions connect and influence one another.

Creative Problem Solving:
You work with complex and sometimes incomplete information, identify patterns and develop practical approaches that turn evidence into meaningful insight.

Agility:
You operate effectively in a rapidly changing communications environment, adjusting priorities and approaches as issues, information and organizational needs evolve.

Drive for Results:
You establish clear expectations, maintain high standards for analytical work and ensure planning, reporting and evaluation contribute to meaningful communications outcomes.

Develop Networks:
You build productive relationships across Communications and Public Engagement, ministry communications teams, executive offices and other partners to strengthen coordination and information sharing.

Qualifications

A university degree in communications, public relations, journalism, political science, public administration, commerce, data analytics or a related field, combined with progressively responsible experience in communications planning, analysis, measurement, evaluation, reporting, issues management or public-sector communications.

Leadership of complex communications planning, intelligence, analysis, measurement or evaluation activities.
Ability to interpret complex information, research and data and translate findings into clear, actionable advice.
Experience developing executive-level briefings, analytical reports, dashboards or recommendations.
Experience advising senior leaders on emerging issues, risks, opportunities and communications considerations.
Leadership experience, including setting priorities, supporting staff development and managing competing demands.
Strong relationship-building skills and experience working across multiple teams, stakeholders or organizational areas.

Preference May Be Given To Candidates Who Demonstrate

Experience developing or leading communications measurement and evaluation frameworks, including performance indicators and outcome measurement.
Experience conducting or overseeing environmental scanning, media analysis, public sentiment analysis or stakeholder intelligence.
Experience developing executive dashboards, analytical reporting or data visualization to support strategic decision-making.
Experience establishing or improving analytical methodologies, reporting standards, information governance or quality assurance practices.
Experience applying technology, automation or artificial intelligence to communications analysis, measurement or reporting.
Experience working in a complex public-sector communications environment.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President HR Shared Services, the VP will integrate HR modernization, platform delivery, process redesign, analytics, AI and automation into a cohesive roadmap with clear governance and measurable outcomes. Key Accountabilities

Own HR modernization delivery: Translate enterprise and HR strategy into an integrated modernization agenda that delivers simpler colleague experiences, greater productivity and measurable business value.
Shape the future of HR: Lead target-state operating model and end-to-end colleague experience design, connecting HR priorities, digital capabilities and new ways of working.
Serve as Executive Product Owner for the HR Solution Train: Set enterprise direction and align priorities across the Acquire Talent, Manage Talent and Support Talent Agile Release Trains.
Lead HR platforms and product delivery: Set direction for HR’s platforms and product portfolio, ensuring products translate HR priorities into scalable colleague solutions.
Simplify HR processes and workflows: Direct feature discovery, workflow redesign, and intelligent automation to simplify HR processes, reduce handoffs, and translate opportunities into delivery-ready investments.
Lead the Analytics Insights & Artificial Intelligence (AI2) team: Set the team's strategic direction and build the capabilities required to deliver HR priorities.
Advance AI, automation and insights: Lead the HR agenda for AI, automation and analytics, identifying high-value opportunities and enabling responsible adoption in partnership with Technology, Data and control functions.
Drive portfolio execution and value: Establish clear priorities, governance and outcome measurement across the HR modernization portfolio, making trade-offs and providing senior leaders with transparent insights on investment, capacity, risks and benefits.
Build exceptional teams and capabilities: Lead and develop multidisciplinary teams across strategy, modernization, product delivery, analytics and enablement, strengthening the capabilities HR needs for the future.

Partner with HR Operating Committee, HR CoEs and HR functional executives to align strategy, investment priorities and target-state outcomes; functional leaders retain policy, program, capability and operational ownership.
Lead HR Product Managers, Finance and portfolio governance teams on business cases, capacity allocation and benefits measurement; investment approvals remain with designated authorities.
Partner across HR and with Technology Engineering, Data, Risk, Privacy, Legal and Compliance to ensure modernization is integrated, responsible and aligned with enterprise standards.

HR and operating model depth: Strong understanding of HR operating models, service delivery and colleague journeys, with experience redesigning processes and end-to-end experiences.
Digital and product orientation: Demonstrated experience with digital platforms, product management, agile delivery and portfolio prioritization, translating strategy into scalable solutions and measurable outcomes.
AI, automation and data fluency: Practical understanding of how AI, automation, data and analytics can transform work and create value, coupled with sound judgement around responsible adoption.
Enterprise influence: Proven ability to establish credibility with senior executives, challenge constructively, navigate competing priorities and create alignment across organizational boundaries.
Transformation at scale: Track record of leading large-scale change from strategy and design through implementation, adoption and benefits realization.
Business leadership: Strong commercial and financial acumen, analytical judgement and executive communication skills, with the ability to turn complexity into clear choices and action.
People leadership: Proven ability to build, lead and develop high-performing, multidisciplinary teams through significant change.
Post-secondary education in business, technology, human resources or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Job Overview

The role provides strategic oversight of the Claims vendor portfolio, advises senior leaders on emerging risks and opportunities, and partners across the organization to optimize vendor performance, resilience and value.

Establishes and leads the vendor management strategy, governance framework and performance standards for Claims, ensuring consistent oversight and alignment with enterprise priorities.
Provides strategic oversight of the Claims vendor portfolio, identifying opportunities, risks, dependencies and performance trends to improve financial, service and operational outcomes.
Establishes vendor evaluation and performance management practices, including segmentation, dashboards, scorecards and action plans, to drive accountability, value realization and continuous improvement.
Leads the evaluation and responsible adoption of AI-enabled vendor capabilities to improve vendor performance, innovation and business outcomes.
Provides strategic oversight of vendor spend, performance and value realization, identifying opportunities to improve financial outcomes and inform Claims planning and business decisions.
Acts as a trusted advisor to senior Claims leaders on vendor strategy, performance, risk, market trends and emerging opportunities, while building strong relationships with enterprise partners and external vendors.
Oversees vendor-related operational, financial, regulatory and continuity risks, including vendor audits, mitigation strategies and enterprise regulatory requirements.

No matter where you are in the organization, you're empowered to make an impact in the lives of our clients and communities.

Leadership is in our DNA at ATB, reflecting our commitment to developing world-class leaders who can truly thrive. Our Leader DNA model sets the standard for how we lead people, drive business performance, and shape a dynamic future. This is the place for purpose-driven individuals ready to deliver impactful leadership every day.

About The Role

As the Director of Market Risk Oversight & Counterparty Credit Risk
, you will provide strategic direction, leadership, and operational success over ATB’s traded financial risks. In an environment where ATB Capital Markets is scaling into a full-service broker, this leadership role bridges the gap between sophisticated trading activities and robust institutional risk boundaries.

You will manage a dedicated team of risk professionals and act as a senior expert advisor across the second line of defense. This role transforms risk oversight from flat compliance into a proactive, data-driven vertical that delivers deep analytical insights, robust independent challenges, and strategic protection of the firm’s bottom line.

Accountabilities

Strategic Leadership & Governance

Develop and execute the long-term vision, strategy, and operating standards for the Trade Floor Market Risk Oversight and Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR) pillars.
Own, maintain, and spearhead limit reviews and calibrations, collaborating with risk and front office stakeholders to ensure risk limits are aligned with risk appetite and business strategy.
Be the subject matter expert for annual and intra-cycle updates of the Board-level Market Risk Management Policy and accompanying Frameworks.
Act as a core member and senior presenter at the Market Risk Oversight Committee (MROC), presenting key market and counterparty credit risk insights and effectively escalating risk postures to the Asset-Liability Committee (ALCO).
Lead the review and implementation of new traded products via the New Initiative Risk Assessment Process (NIRAP) to safely onboard new capital market instruments and product lines.
Design, implement, and execute a rigorous 2nd line control framework to continuously validate market risk and counterparty credit risk models via systematic backtesting.

Market Risk Oversight & Analytics

Oversee independent daily monitoring and granular analysis of desk-level trading risks across traded securities and derivatives products (including Fixed Income, Interest Rates, Foreign Exchange, Equities, and Commodities).
Ensure absolute integrity of end-of-day (EOD) and intra-day risk reporting metrics, including Value-at-Risk (VaR), Stressed VaR (SVaR), sensitivities/Greeks (DV01, CS01), and Notional limits.
Direct real-time limit excess management and breach escalation protocols across first and second lines of defense.
Drive the end-to-end framework for ensuring that market risk models, measurements, and risk engines are structurally sound, comprehensive, and accurate.
Establish robust processes and controls to guarantee that all risk factors—specifically complex nuances like basis risk (including tenor, currency, and index basis mismatches), volatility smiles, and correlation breakdowns—are fully captured, mapped, and measured
Lead the development and enhancement of trade floor and counterparty credit risk reporting and analytics to foster proactive risk management.
Strengthen and maintain the robustness of market risk frameworks by effectively identifying and capturing risks across unique, complex, and bespoke business lines (e.g., equity bought deals, off-market trades)

Counterparty Credit Risk Oversight

Formulate and enforce the strategic 2nd line framework for all traded credit exposures, including Potential Future Exposure (PFE) profiles, single name issuer risk and settlement risk.
Ensure the completeness, accuracy, and rigorous governance of model inputs feeding into counterparty credit risk engines, including credit curve mappings, ensuring that Potential Future Exposure (PFE) model parameters are mathematically sound and reflective of current market dynamics
Monitor portfolio concentrations and counterparty credit updates across Issuer Risk, Repo, Derivatives, and Collateral frameworks.
Strengthen Counterparty Credit Risk policies & frameworks by aligning with industry and regulatory best practices.

Required Qualifications

Skills, experience & requirements

A University degree in Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Financial Engineering, or a highly quantitative discipline.
8+ years of progressive experience working within financial markets in either a 1st line (Front Office/Execution) or 2nd line (Risk Management) financial risk role.
Professional certifications such as FRM, CFA, or PRMIA are a strong asset.

Core Technical Skills

Mastered expertise in multi-asset Capital Markets financial instruments (FICC derivatives, equities, repo, debt capital markets).
Advanced understanding of derivative pricing, risk-neutral and real-world simulation modeling frameworks, Monte Carlo engines, and volatility skews/smiles.
In-depth practical knowledge of risk systems, specifically Murex and Bloomberg (MARS/TOMS).
Quantitative data proficiency utilizing tools like Python, SQL, and Google BigQuery (DEEP architecture).

Leadership & Interpersonal Attributes

Proven people leader capable of mentoring high-performing analysts and managers, cultivating technical excellence, and fostering a collaborative, psychological safe culture.
Elite stakeholder management and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to deliver a credible, robust challenge to first-line business line heads and traders.

A resume only goes so far in expressing who you are and the unique perspectives you bring. If you believe your skills and experience align with the role—but you might not check all the boxes—we want to hear from you. We encourage candidates from all work backgrounds, equity-seeking communities and experience levels to apply. If you’re seeking a career where your drive, perspective and growth are celebrated, we want to hear from you.

We’re dedicated to building a workforce reflective of those within our communities, and a culture where our team members are equipped with what they need to succeed—their way. Part of creating an inclusive workplace is recognizing our role in advancing Truth and Reconciliation. We are committed to meeting and exceeding the standards set out in the Partnership Accreditation in Indigenous Relations program created by the Canadian Council for Indigenous Business.
